table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: policy lookup by leave type when validating requests; is_active: filtering active policies for entitlement resolution

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: employee self-service listing of own requests; status: manager approval queues filtered by status; start_date, end_date: date-range queries and overlap detection; leave_type_id: filtering by leave type

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: balance lookup for an employee; policy_id: balance lookup by policy; fiscal_year: accrual/entitlement scoping per fiscal year; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique balance row resolution

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: inbox listing per recipient; status: pending/sent delivery fanout queries; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: lookup of notifications for a given entity

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail lookup for a specific entity; performed_by: audit lookup by actor; performed_at: time-range audit reports; action: filtering by action type

All use UUID string ids (BaseEntity id/created_at/updated_at). leave_requests.status is a string enum (see open question on LeaveStatus values). leave_balances.used_days/remaining_days are numeric (rounding semantics open). audit_logs.old_values/new_values are JSONB. notifications.status uses PENDING/SENT/READ/ARCHIVED. Six repository interfaces named with concrete Knex/pg-backed implementations. No DDL written — migrations generated by code agent from these specs.

open_questions.question: LeaveStatus enum value discrepancy: DOMAIN.md defines DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED, while root ARCHITECTURE.md uses PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED. Which set is authoritative for the leave_requests.status field and shared types?
open_questions.impact: Affects the status column values, the shared LeaveStatus type in src/shared/types/leave.types.ts, manager approval-queue queries, and any status-transition validation. Choosing one set now and changing later requires a data migration and type churn.
candidate_options: Use DOMAIN.md set (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED) — richer draft/submitted lifecycle
Use ARCHITECTURE.md set (PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED) — simpler, no draft state

open_questions.question: How are leave_balances.used_days and remaining_days computed, rounded, and bounded when a request is approved (e.g. partial-day requests, half-day rounding, negative-balance guard)?
open_questions.impact: This is a foundational counting/rounding/range semantic that must hold identically across the approval service, the balance commitDays repository method, and any accrual scheduler. Asserting one rounding direction in a single query while leaving the rest implicit risks the BR-001 anti-pattern (inconsistent balance math across call sites).
candidate_options: Whole-day granularity only; reject fractional-day requests
Half-day granularity (0.5 steps); round to nearest 0.5
Decimal days with fixed 2-decimal rounding (round half up)
Decimal days with fixed 2-decimal rounding (round half down)

open_questions.question: Should concrete repositories use Knex query builder or raw pg (parameterized SQL) against the shared pg.Pool?
open_questions.impact: Determines the implementation style of every repository and the base repository helper. Knex is declared for migrations; connection.ts currently exposes a raw pg.Pool. The choice affects query construction, transaction client passing, and test mocking.
candidate_options: Knex query builder (consistent with ADR migrations + thin repository layer)
Raw pg parameterized SQL (matches existing connection.ts Pool exposure)
Knex for migrations only; raw pg for repository queries

transaction_contract: The service owns the unit of work; the data-access layer acquires the connection. A single IUnitOfWork.withTransaction<T>(fn: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>) is the ONLY place issuing BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. Every repository method that must join a caller's transaction takes an OPTIONAL PoolClient as its last parameter (defaulting to the shared pg.Pool when omitted). The calling service acquires a client via withTransaction, passes it to each participating repository call (e.g. leave_requests.updateStatus + leave_balances.commitDays + audit_logs.record), then COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Nested withTransaction reuses an already-supplied client instead of opening a second transaction. This contract is REQUIRED for the approve/reject flow (status change + balance update + audit row must be atomic).
